issues: Archive-tier trap overlaps with -004 but tests different facts (full snapshots vs retention under 90 days).

Blind dispute resolved: the key is decidable from documented properties, not prices: the archive tier converts incremental snapshots to full snapshots, has a 90-day minimum archive period billed on early delete, is described as lower cost 'for snapshots that you plan to store for 90 days or longer', restores take up to 72 hours (fails 'a few hours'), and AWS Backup cold storage needs total retention of 90 days or greater. With 30-day retention, none of the archive options help. Wrong option C's why is correct. The stem is slightly leading ('an engineer wants to') but fine.

Blind dispute confirmed: both the key (cold after 30 days) and wrong option A (cold after 1 day) reach cold storage for the 730-day retention, so the qualifier 'LOWEST storage cost' does not clearly separate them for a candidate who does not know the AWS Backup full-backup behavior.

The distinction is documented (creating a backup plan page: transition after 1 day makes AWS Backup create another warm full backup; AWS Backup recommends not moving to cold until at least 8 days), but 'adds cost' is an inference and the stem never mentions incremental versus full behavior. Option A can be defended as cheaper.
suggestedFix: Replace wrong option A with a setting that clearly fails a stated requirement: 'Move backups to cold storage after 30 days and set the total retention period to 60 days' (why: retention shorter than the two years required, and cold storage needs a total retention of 90 days or greater). Keep the key and the existing evidence.

issues: Similar key/distractor structure to cold-cellar-001 and backup-archive-007 (Deep Archive vs Instant Retrieval for rarely read records); the EBS-to-S3 twist keeps it distinct enough.
Second half (Deep Archive vs Glacier Instant Retrieval) repeats cold-cellar-001/-006 logic; acceptable. Evidence quote from sgw-tape supports a wrong option rather than the key; harmless.

Key (EBS Snapshots Archive) is documented: 'up to 75 percent lower snapshot storage costs for snapshots that you plan to store for 90 days or longer and that you rarely need to access', 'only snapshot of a volume, such as end-of-project snapshots'; wait of days fits the 72-hour restore.

Blind dispute resolved: wrong option C ('copy the snapshot to an S3 Glacier Deep Archive bucket by using the Amazon S3 console') is an impossible action (snapshots are stored in S3 buckets you cannot access; the page says you cannot use the S3 console or API on snapshots). It is presented as a possible action, and a candidate could defend 'copy the data to Deep Archive' as cheaper.
suggestedFix: Replace option C with a feasible but non-optimal distractor, e.g. 'Copy the snapshot to a second AWS Region and keep it in the standard tier' (why: adds a second copy and stays in the standard tier, which costs more than the archive tier for a snapshot kept 90 days or longer and rarely accessed). Drop the S3-console evidence quote or keep it only as background.
